title: GS21 industry sign x standardized leverage (mean zero) with a continuous firm-level debt capacity: six mirrored types on the gs_level ladder, exposure gs_bv_f b~ at loadings +-0.05 / 0.1 / 0.15, coupons drawn from [0.1, 0.9], price 2.5
question: The mean-zero version of gvyslq: does the product of the industry sign and the firm's standardized leverage, with no additive part, give GS21 room and a gap as the productivity version (gvysz2) does?
notes:
WHY (2026-11-02). The industry sign x financial leverage interaction with a firm-level, continuously drawn debt capacity (gs_fixcs 2, coupon from the 16 grid nodes in [0.1, 0.9], fixed for life). The fixed-coupon TYPE version (gvysl15/20) had room under 1% because two industries x three coupons are six perfectly observed groups the linear model prices directly. Six mirrored industry types on the gs_level ladder 0.5..2.0 (size reveals the sign in part), no compensation. The exposure is gs_bv_f b~, mean zero across firms (gvysz2's construction with leverage in place of productivity). Loadings [-0.35, -0.2, -0.1, 0.1, 0.2, 0.35].

PRECOMMITMENT STATUS: precommitted=false; ids filled from the Quest build log by the solve script before any seed runs.

RERUN (2026-11-05): gvyslz's +0.2 and +0.35 types hit the sweep cap; gvyslq (exposure proportional to the coupon, +-0.05/0.1/0.15) converged and gave room 10-41% and a fair gap of +0.017 (t 4.0, ten of ten) on linear ceilings of 0.4-1.1. This is the mean-zero version at gvyslq's loadings. PREDICTION (2026-11-02): room 30% or more (gvysz2, the same construction on productivity: 22-66%) and a fair gap at or above +0.029. FALSIFIED if room is at or below 10% on three seeds.
